title: StrictLocalInjectiveSourceTransition
statement:
For $f:X\to S$, a geometric point $s$, $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(X_{et}))$,
$n\in\mathbf Z$, a specified bounded-below injective complex $J$ and $q:K\cong QJ$,
let $A_i$ be the explicitly constructed comparison
[def-weil-pbc-strict-local-injective-source-comparison]. Let $F$ be the derived
source-neighbourhood functor [def-weil-pbc-canonical-derived-cohomology-germs] and
$r_a$ the termwise restriction [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sections-pullback-comparison].
For every neighbourhood arrow $a:i\to j$, $F(a)\,A_i=A_j\,r_a$. There is no limit
or cone-leg assertion.

proof.text: The right-derived unit and localization on Hom into the K-injective direct image commute with precomposition. The Hom-complex map is the map induced by the free sheaf of the neighbourhood arrow. Evaluation at the free generator identifies it with the direct-image sections restriction, by Yoneda naturality.

Unit compatibility of the localization-restriction comparison identifies this chain restriction with sectionsPullbackNat followed by upperStarComp.inv. Take homology and use naturality of its localization comparison to obtain F(a) A_i = A_j r_a. Identity arrows and zero complexes give identity and zero chain maps.
